problem: VLN-CE agents trained end-to-end on low-level actions or waypoints in continuous Habitat environments reached less than half the success rate of agents in the nav-graph VLN setting, even though both use the same R2R instructions and paths. It was unknown whether VLN agents could transfer to continuous environments, and which differences between the two settings cause the performance loss.
motivation: The low VLN-CE performance was usually blamed on the difficulty of learning navigation and language grounding jointly over long horizons. That leaves two options: build better VLN-CE models, or reuse the strong models already developed for topological VLN. Following the sim-2-real work of Anderson et al., the authors emulate the VLN action and observation space inside VLN-CE. They use this to measure how much performance each source of the gap costs: dataset subset, visual rendering, navigation and subgoal generation.
key_idea: A modular harness lets a nav-graph-trained VLN agent (Recurrent VLN↻BERT) run in VLN-CE. A learned subgoal generation module (panoramic RGB + 360° laser scan) produces the candidate waypoints the agent chooses from, and a map-based local planner executes each choice with low-level actions. The harness also isolates each step of the VLN→VLN-CE transfer so its performance cost can be quantified.
insight:
Starting from VLN, the Val-Unseen SR drop decomposes as follows (the dataset and navigation terms are the text's own tally; its '1 SR' visual term is inconsistent with Table 2, so it is taken from Table 2 here):
- 1 SR from the VLN-CE data subset.
- A visual gap from reconstructed renders: zero-shot swap costs 3 SR (61→58, Table 2 rows 1 vs 2); retraining on Habitat renders recovers all but 1 SR (60 vs 61). The zero-shot swap costs 10-13 SR in seen environments, which suggests VLN agents overfit to visual features.
- 5 SR from realistic navigation. The Oracle Policy matches teleportation (60 vs 60 SR), but the local policy has a long tail of navigation errors above 0.5 m, 15x more often than the oracle.
- 12 SR from predicted subgoals, the dominant term. The coarse polar prediction space alone costs 6 SR even with perfect predictions.
Half of the subgoal gap (6 SR) comes from episodes with more than 1.0 m elevation change (stairs). The SGM has a recall problem there because 2D laser free-space poorly predicts elevation-changing subgoals. Even a greedy oracle selector reaches only 38% on such Val-Train episodes, and the final agent gets 19 vs 48 SR on high- vs low-elevation Val-Unseen episodes. SGM ablations show that training on Habitat-rendered RGB (+3 SR) and a 360° instead of 270° laser scan (+5 SR) together give +8 SR Val-Unseen over Anderson et al.'s SGM. Fine-tuning the VLN agent on SGM candidates recovers only 2 SR.
method: Core VLN agent: Recurrent VLN↻BERT (PREVALENT init). It is retrained on panoramas rendered from Habitat 3D reconstructions at nav-graph node poses (36 views, 3 elevations × 12 headings, ResNet-152 Places365 features) to close the visual domain gap ('rt-VLN↻BERT').

Subgoal Generation Module (SGM, adapted from Anderson et al. sim-2-real): a U-Net fuses panoramic ResNet-152 RGB features with a 24×48 radial obstacle map from an emulated 360° 2D laser scanner (4.8 m range, 0.2 m / 7.5° bins). It predicts a radial subgoal heat map; Gaussian NMS then selects the top k=5 (r,θ) candidates. It is trained with Sinkhorn divergence to nav-graph neighbors, using Habitat-rendered RGB.

Local Policy (after Chaplot et al.): builds a per-target local occupancy map from projected egocentric depth (unexplored area treated as free) and plans with the Fast Marching Method to a point 0.25 m ahead. It greedily decodes FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° actions and stops within 0.15 m of the target or after 40 actions.

Oracle diagnostics (not VLN-CE admissible): teleportation with heading snapped to 30°, an A* Oracle Policy on the navmesh, nav-graph subgoals with graph re-localization to the nearest node, and 'Optimal SGM' (nav-graph subgoals discretized into the SGM polar bins).

Fine-tuning in VLN-CE: the rt-VLN↻BERT is trained by teacher-forced imitation learning over online SGM candidates, with the target being the candidate that greedily minimizes geodesic distance to the goal. Settings: cross-entropy loss, batch 12, lr 1e-7, early stopping, about 12 GPU-hours.

Stepwise gap analysis: agents are evaluated while moving progressively from VLN to VLN-CE (dataset subset → reconstructed vision → navigation policy → predicted subgoals), followed by an elevation-stratified failure analysis.

setting.backbone: Recurrent VLN↻BERT (PREVALENT init, ResNet-152 Places365 features; retrained on Habitat renders, fine-tuned in VLN-CE) + U-Net subgoal generation module + non-learned FMM mapping/planning local policy
setting.training_data: R2R train, used to retrain VLN↻BERT with official codebase/PREVALENT init on Habitat-rendered panoramas at nav-graph node poses. SGM trained on MP3D nav-graph node neighbors (Val-Unseen nodes held out) with Habitat-rendered RGB + emulated laser scans. Fine-tuning by imitation learning on R2R-CE train episodes with online SGM candidates (~12 GPU-hours).
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) for agent and SGM + emulated 360° 2D laser scan (SGM) + egocentric depth for local occupancy mapping (local policy); relative subgoal targets (r,θ)
setting.action_space: select among 5 predicted subgoal candidates (r,θ); executed by local policy with low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN-LEFT/RIGHT 15° / STOP (max 40 actions per subgoal)
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE); Matterport3D simulator for VLN diagnostics
setting.privileged: none for the final agent, though it adds a 360° 2D laser scanner sensor beyond the standard VLN-CE sensors. Diagnostic variants use GT nav-graph subgoals, an A* navmesh oracle policy, or teleportation.

results: The final transfer agent reaches 44 SR / 37 SPL on the R2R-CE (VLN-CE) test leaderboard and 43 SR / 36 SPL on Val-Unseen. It beats the previous best, HPN+DN (32 SR test, 36 SR val-unseen, which needed 7000+ GPU-hours), by +12 SR on test with about 12 GPU-hours of fine-tuning. SPL gains are smaller (37 vs 30 test; 36 vs 34 val-unseen). The transfer still loses about 18 SR relative to VLN↻BERT in nav-graph VLN (61→43 Val-Unseen), mostly from subgoal candidate generation (12 SR), with navigation errors costing 5 SR.
limitations: The subgoal generation module fails to propose elevation-changing (stairs) subgoals, because 2D laser free-space is a poor cue for them. The final agent gets only 19 SR vs 48 SR on high- vs low-elevation Val-Unseen episodes.
A large gap to nav-graph performance remains (43 vs 55-60 SR Val-Unseen), and fine-tuning on SGM candidates recovers only 2 SR. The coarse polar prediction space alone costs 6 SR.

The approach relies on an added 360° 2D laser scanner and panoramic RGB beyond standard VLN-CE sensing. The local policy also has a long tail of navigation failures (5.73% of subgoal navigations end more than 1.0 m away on Val-Unseen).
